paper: Holberg et al. 2016, MNRAS 462, 2295 (system description only)
quote: G107-70AB is also part of a quadruple system including G107-69, itself a very close astrometric binary with an sDM primary with a 0.94 yr orbital period (Harrington, Christy & Strand, 1981).
notes: Ab is the unseen astrometric companion of the sdM5 star G 107-69 = GJ 275.2 A (Harrington et al. 1981, P = 0.94 yr). It has never been detected directly; no spectrum, Teff or luminosity exists. The MSC's 'DA' for it is not a spectral classification of an observed object (MSC flags the pair type 'A?' and comments 'GJ 275.2A But RUWE=1.1'), and SIMBAD lists G 107-69 as M4V only. The DA white dwarfs of this system are Ba/Bb (G 107-70AB = WD 0727+482). Leave blank.

notes: Converted from log L/Lsun = -4.01 (no uncertainty printed on log L). Photometric fit with the trigonometric parallax; log g 7.86, M = 0.50 Msun. Mapped Ba = Limoges' A (the brighter, MV 14.51). Holberg et al. 2016 Table 3 gives the pair as 0727+482.1: Teff 4934(81), log g 7.89, 0.599 Msun, Mbol 14.79 and 0727+482.2: 4926(85), 8.10, 0.634 Msun, Mbol 15.09 -> log L -4.02 / -4.14 with Mbol_sun = 4.75, consistent. What these components actually are: G 107-70 = WD 0727+482 = LHS 230, a resolved double white dwarf (0.6 arcsec, P ~ 18.8-20.5 yr; Nelan et al. 2015 astrometric masses 0.634 and 0.599 Msun per Holberg); both are cool H-atmosphere white dwarfs. Spectral type: Limoges 'DA', Holberg 'DA10.0' (A) and 'DA10.1' (B), SIMBAD 'DA+DA'; the MSC's DC9 is older. Earlier Bergeron et al. 1989 values quoted in the literature (7470/6920 K) are superseded.

L converted from the printed Mbol = 14.44 with Mbol_sun = 4.75 (the Montreal-table convention stated by Limoges et al. 2015): log L = -3.876. Holberg does not print L itself; with Mbol_sun = 4.74 L would be 1.32e-4. GJ 171.2 B = HD 283750B = WD 0433+270 = G 39-27 (SIMBAD). Spectral type is disputed: Holberg DA9.0, Limoges 2015 DA, SIMBAD and the MSC DC8. Gentile Fusillo et al. 2021 (VizieR J/MNRAS/508/3877, WDJ043644.90+270951.52, Gaia plx 57.47 mas) gives pure-H TeffH = 5534 +/- 29 K, log g = 8.022 +/- 0.019, M = 0.598 +/- 0.011 Msun (He: 5421 K, 7.944, 0.536 Msun); no L. DOUBT: Limoges et al. 2015 Table 5 prints a different, directly tabulated value, '04367+2709 DA 5920 (112) 8.87 (0.19) 1.13 (0.10) H 15.68 -4.34 16.6 (0.8) 60.2 ( 2.9) 9.75 1 0433+270' (log L = -4.34, L = 4.6e-5), from a spectroscopic fit giving an implausible 1.13 Msun; it disagrees with both Holberg (0.62 Msun) and the Gaia-parallax photometric fit (0.60 Msun), so the Holberg value is preferred here.
